findings.title: HTML_TAGS regex misses closing tags and uppercase tags
findings.body:
The regex `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` only matches opening tags whose name consists of lowercase ASCII letters. Closing tags like `

` and uppercase tags like `
` will not be detected. The `containsHtml` decision gates whether POLICY_SOME_HTML or POLICY_NO_HTML is applied to translations, so any English source that contains only closing tags or uppercase tags will be treated as having no HTML. The translation will then be sanitized with POLICY_NO_HTML, which will escape those tags (e.g., `

` becomes `</p>`), making them appear as literal text in the rendered UI.

findings.title: Method name typo `santizeAnchors`
findings.body: The method is named `santizeAnchors` (missing 'i'). Should be `sanitizeAnchors`. This is cosmetic but reflects on code quality.

findings.title: Missing English file throws RuntimeException, crashing the verifier
findings.body: When the English counterpart file cannot be found (e.g., for a brand new translation that has no `_en.properties` source yet, or for a locale like `es_419` whose suffix contains digits and so does not match the locale-detection regex on line 75), the FileInputStream constructor throws FileNotFoundException, which is caught and rewrapped as `new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)`. Because `verifySafeHtml` does not declare any checked exceptions and `verify()` only catches `IOException`, this RuntimeException propagates out of the Mojo, bypassing the normal MojoExecutionException error path. The result is that any file whose English source is missing will abort the entire verification, instead of producing a clean message.

findings.title: Locale-suffix regex doesn't accept digits, blocking non-Latin locale files
findings.body: The path translation `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` only matches locale suffixes that consist entirely of ASCII letters, hyphen and underscore. BCP-47 derived locales that include digits (e.g. `es_419`, `en_US_POSIX`, or numeric region sub-tags) will not match the regex, so `replaceAll` is a no-op and `englishFile` equals `file`. The code then tries to load the same file as its own English source and either crashes (because the regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*` excludes digits) or silently validates a translation against itself. The character class also includes the underscore, which is fragile when suffixes themselves contain underscores (e.g. `zh_CN`).

findings.title: Magic string `<!-- -->` removed unconditionally from sanitized output
findings.body: After `policy.sanitize(value)` and `unescapeHtml4`, the code does `sanitized = sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")`. This hardcoded string is presumed to be what the OWASP sanitizer inserts to disambiguate content, but the OWASP library is not part of the project's source, so this is an undocumented and version-dependent contract. If a future OWASP release inserts a different placeholder (e.g. `<!---->` without space, `<!---->`, or HTML-escaped form), the replacement will silently stop working and the sanitizer output will be reported as illegal HTML for any translation containing double curly braces. Worse, the replacement is applied unconditionally even when the original `value` legitimately contains the substring `<!-- -->`, in which case legitimate comments are silently stripped and the comparison will erroneously consider the value 'clean'.

findings.title: replaceFirst in santizeAnchors operates on a value mutated by previous iterations
findings.body: In `santizeAnchors`, the Matcher is constructed from the original `value`, so `matcher.find()` continues to identify anchors at their original positions even after the body of the loop has replaced earlier occurrences in `value`. When the value contains the same anchor twice (e.g. two `<a href="X">`), the first iteration replaces the first occurrence in the (still identical) value, but the second iteration tries `value.replaceFirst(englishMatcher.group(), "")` on the already-shortened string, which no longer contains that anchor at that position. The replacement becomes a no-op, the loop advances to the next match in the original string, and the second anchor ends up compared against the next English anchor (or causes a spurious 'did not find anchor tag' message). The logic should either rebuild the Matcher after each replacement or use indices rather than `replaceFirst` to align modifications.

findings.title: POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML should be static final
findings.body: `PolicyFactory POLICY_SOME_HTML = new org.owasp.html.HtmlPolicyBuilder()...toFactory();` and the corresponding `POLICY_NO_HTML` are declared as instance fields on a class that has only instance state (`file`, `messages`). They should be `private static final` so they are constructed once per JVM rather than per VerifyMessageProperties instance and so that the class clearly expresses they are constants.

findings.title: Comment about `<!-- -->` placement is unclear and possibly wrong
findings.body: The block comment on lines 96-97 reads `// Sanitizer will add them when there are double curly braces`, where 'them' is ambiguous (HTML comments? entities?). The actual rationale is that the OWASP policy inserts an HTML comment to separate ambiguous sequences, not specifically 'when there are double curly braces'. Anyone reading this code in the future will not understand the dependency on OWASP's exact placeholder format. A short, accurate comment (and ideally an OWASP API that exposes skipped content) would prevent future breakage.

findings.title: No test coverage for closing/uppercase HTML tags or English missing file
findings.body:
The new tests cover duplicate keys, illegal HTML tags in an English file (`illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`), a non-English file with `` (noHtml_de.properties) and a changed anchor (`changedAnchor_de.properties`). They do not cover the scenarios where the English source contains only a closing tag (e.g. `

`), only uppercase tags, a translation that is missing keys present in the English source, an English source file that is missing entirely, or translations where the order of identical anchors differs. Given that the verifier's correctness depends on these edge cases, at least one negative test for 'English has only closing tags -> POLICY_NO_HTML is wrongly applied' should be added.
